feed.title: NPR Topics: Health
feed.subtitle: Comprehensive health news from NPR. Follow for updates on medical research, wellness trends, public health policy, patient care and healthcare systems.

entry.title: Drone photo award winners: Far-out landscapes. Ship recycling. Rugs, rugs rugs!
entry.summary: The Siena Drone Photo Awards for 2026 offer breathtaking bird's-eye views of our planet, revealing landscapes, livelihoods and human stories often invisible from the ground.

entry.title: Do you have seasonal affective disorder? How to tell — and what to do about it
entry.summary: The syndrome can make people feel like a "hibernating bear," says Dr. Norman Rosenthal, who published the first research on SAD. He explains how to identify the symptoms and what to do to feel better.

entry.title: Nearly 2 out of 3 teens and tweens use AI chatbots, new research shows
entry.summary: Most kids say they use chatbots for help with homework and when they're stressed, lonely, or anxious. And how they use chatbots is tied to their mental health.

entry.title: Florida sees spike in dengue fever cases
entry.summary: Florida is seeing a record number of dengue fever cases this year as the tropical disease thrives in warming climates.

entry.title: What killed 500-plus penguins? How scientists solved the mystery
entry.summary: The penguins that perished lived on the Danger Islands in Antarctica. The prime suspect was avian flu. Researchers were surprised by what they found.

entry.title: Lost your spark? The "silent sister" of depression, and a quiz to spot her
entry.summary: Always busy, but rarely joyful? Allison Aubrey and Juana Summers discuss a tool to spot "high functioning depression."

entry.title: Ahead of midterms, Missourians defend transgender healthcare
entry.summary: The campaign to defend access to transgender healthcare for young people in Missouri is taking an unhurried approach to talking with voters about the proposed ban.

entry.title: New blood test can detect changes associated with Alzheimer's disease
entry.summary: Brain changes associated with Alzheimer's disease can be detected by a new type of blood test -- and a growing number of patients are asking their doctors about it.

entry.title: Eleven states cut Medicaid coverage for refugees who are pregnant or children
entry.summary: When Congress cut Medicaid benefits for refugees who are in the U.S. legally, most states allowed them to continue for children and pregnant women. Arizona and 10 others did not.

entry.title: Trump administration will allow pharmacies to make popular peptides
entry.summary: The Department of Health and Human Services will let small compounding pharmacies make six peptides that haven't been approved by the Food and Drug Administration. It may not be enough to meet demand.
